memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Joseph went and told Pharaoh, 'My father and brothers, with their flocks and herds and everything they own, have come from the land of Canaan and are now in Goshen.' He chose five of his brothers and presented them before Pharaoh." — Gen 47:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joseph does exactly what he said he would do. He goes to Pharaoh, tells him plainly where his family has come from and what they have brought, and then presents five of his brothers in person.

Notice that he presents them. These are shepherds from a famine-struck land, standing in the most powerful court on earth, and Joseph is not embarrassed by them. He does not leave them waiting outside while he negotiates. He brings them in and stands them before the king.

Think about who these men are. They sold him. They are the reason he spent years as a slave and a prisoner. And here he is, using every bit of the standing he has earned to open a door for them.

Forgiveness that stops at "I no longer hold it against you" is real but incomplete. Joseph goes further — he actively uses his position for their good.

This is the pattern of Christ's love for us, only immeasurably greater. He does not merely forgive us and leave us outside the door. He presents us. He brings us before the Father as His own, and He lives to intercede for us there (Heb 7:25).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there someone you have forgiven but not yet actively blessed?
2. How could you use your position, whatever it is, to open a door for someone else?
3. What does it mean to you that Christ presents you before the Father?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Jesus does not merely forgive me but brings me before You as His own. Help me use whatever standing I have to open doors for others, especially those who have wronged me. Amen.
